title: How Swiss tables work in Go built-in map
summary: This article explains the internal implementation of Swiss tables in Go's built-in map, covering how the hash table algorithm works, its memory efficiency improvements, and the performance benefits over traditional open addressing schemes used in earlier Go versions.
problem_solved: Provides understanding of how Go implements efficient hash maps using Swiss table algorithm for better cache locality and reduced memory overhead.
why_valuable: Helps Go developers understand map internals to write more performant code and debug hash-related issues by knowing how collisions, rehashing, and memory layout work under the hood.
